requiredFindings.title: The freshness check runs before the mode is set, so directory creation now depends on the process umask's owner-search bit
requiredFindings.detail: fresh_empty_directory opens "." relative to the new directory (needs search permission) before set_permissions(0700), while the directory still has its umask-derived mkdirat mode. Under umasks 177, 133, 111 and 377 (measured) create_exclusive_directory and create_private_directory now fail with PermissionDenied and leave a 0600/0400 directory (retry: AlreadyExists); the accepted 454 r2 base returns a 0700 directory in each case. The trailing set_permissions(0700) exists so the final mode does not depend on the umask. The file creator is unaffected.
requiredFindings.fix: Make the check need only permissions already held: e.g. fstat owner and link count, set 0700 on the (euid-owned) descriptor, then scan; or scan through a descriptor that needs only the read access already held. Reviewer variant R1 (the check moved after the mode change) passes both owner tests and every probe and yields 0700 under every umask 022-377. Add a test that fails on this candidate (restrictive umask in an isolated child process, or a direct check on a 0600 fixture if the scan no longer needs search).

requiredFindings.title: The directory scan treats a readdir error as end of directory
requiredFindings.detail: readdir returns NULL at end of stream and on error; only errno distinguishes them (POSIX: set errno to 0 before the call, check it after NULL; Rust std does so). The loop breaks on any NULL and returns Ok when no other entry was seen, so a readdir failure reports 'contains only . and ..' without having read the directory: a fail-open in the check this unit adds. On APFS the link-count test already refuses static contents, limiting exposure to entries added after fstat; on Linux (method compiled and public) ext4/xfs link counts exclude files, so the scan is the only file-content check.
requiredFindings.fix: Clear errno before each readdir; on NULL with errno != 0 return that error. Keep closedir on every path.

observations.summary: The freshness check is not pinned by owner tests: all six variants M1-M6 pass both owner tests. Add direct fresh_empty_directory tests like F1-F4. On APFS M2 and M4 each survive alone because the two tests overlap.

Link count 2 is a filesystem convention: APFS counts every entry (measured), ext4/xfs count subdirectories, btrfs reports 1 for every directory (this method would refuse every new directory there, fail-closed). Linux not replayed.

Identity still not proven: a same-euid empty directory with link count 2 substituted in the window is accepted, then set 0700 and ACL-sampled; acceptable as the same principal. The create_exclusive_directory doc does not mention the check or its AlreadyExists refusal (security reports it as Create(AlreadyExists), like an existing name).

Cost convention: one edge for the scan (openat '.', fdopendir, getdirentries, closedir) matches the append's outer-API convention; the capture counts native stat output buffers in bytes, this fstat buffer is not counted (directory cost bytes 0).
unsafe close(scan) lacks a SAFETY comment; the error is read after close (harmless if close succeeds; capture first).

Security test lacks directory existing-entry/symlink cases; single_component error text says 'file'; residual entry after refusal and retry AlreadyExists; public unaccounted create_exclusive_*; openat mode style nit; unused From impls and nested WorkFailure.
